cards.explanation: The answer is John the Baptist risen from the dead. Herod tells his servants, "This is John the Baptist; he has risen from the dead! That is why miraculous powers are at work in him." (Matthew 14:2). Herod hears the reports and lands on a conclusion faster than anybody reading half a group chat, friends. Notice he's the one connecting the dots here, and he lands on John.

The word is lawful. John had been telling Herod, "It is not lawful for you to have her." (Matthew 14:4). Herodias was Herod's brother Philip's wife, and John said it to Herod himself. Matthew tells us Herod arrested him, bound him and put him in prison on account of her.

What holds Herod back is that he's afraid of the people. Matthew says, "Although Herod wanted to kill John, he was afraid of the people, because they regarded John as a prophet." (Matthew 14:5). Here's a ruler with a prison, friends, and he's still watching the crowd. The text gives the reason right there: the people regarded John as a prophet.

The answer is False. Matthew says the daughter of Herodias danced before them "…and pleased Herod" (Matthew 14:6). The next verse shows how much, because he promises with an oath to give her whatever she asks (Matthew 14:7). It was his birthday, and he made a big promise.

Herod promised her whatever she asked. He was so pleased that he "…promised with an oath to give to her whatever she asked." (Matthew 14:7). That's a blank check, friends, with a crowd of guests watching him sign it. He didn't name a limit, and an oath is a heavy thing to attach to that.

The answer is True. Matthew says she was "Prompted by her mother…" (Matthew 14:8). So her mother is the one who prompted her before the girl tells Herod what she wants. The text tells us who prompted her, and that's all it tells us. It doesn't say how or what was said between them.

Herod is grieved. Matthew says, "The king was grieved, but because of his oaths and his guests, he ordered that her wish be granted" (Matthew 14:9). Herod is grieved, and he still gives the order. This is a heavy part of the story, friends, so we'll let it sit as it is.

The word is disciples. Matthew says, "Then John’s disciples came and took his body and buried it." (Matthew 14:12). These are the people who had followed John. I think this is a tender moment, friends. They came and cared for his body.

The answer is True. Matthew says, "And they went and informed Jesus." (Matthew 14:12). They buried John's body, and then they took the news to Jesus. I think this one hurts, friends. The text only says they went and told Him.
